protocol.name: gex_window_placement_v1

protocol.description:
A window system whose windows have real coordinates -- Win32 under Wine, X11 override-redirect windows -- decides where each window is and what is above what, and its programs depend on that being true on screen: a taskbar at the bottom edge, a Start menu above it, a tooltip above the window it describes, a click landing on the window the program believes is there. xdg_shell has no positions and no cross-client stacking, so a surface that needs both says so here.
A surface with a placement object is "placed": the compositor shows it at the position its client set, stacks it where its client asked, does not cascade it, size it, raise it on click or give it the keyboard on its own initiative. A surface without one keeps the compositor's own layout.
Coordinates are in the output's pixels, (0, 0) its top-left corner -- the same space the client's own window system uses for a single screen.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Placement objects already made are unaffected.

request.name: get_placement
request.description: The surface keeps whatever role it has or will be given (an xdg_toplevel, typically). It is placed from its next commit with a buffer until the placement object is destroyed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface goes back to the compositor's own layout.

request.name: set_position

description.summary: where the surface's top-left corner is

request.description: In output pixels. Takes effect at once: moving a window does not need new contents.

request.name: set_stack_id

description.summary: name the surface for stacking requests

request.description: A number other placed surfaces -- of this client or another -- can name in place_below. Ids are the client window system's own (a Win32 window handle, an X window id), so they are shared by every client of one session. Zero is no id.

request.name: place_below
request.description: Put the surface directly below the placed surface whose stack id is `sibling`, within the layer. Zero puts it at the top of its layer, 0xffffffff at the bottom. A sibling the compositor does not know (not mapped yet, or gone) counts as zero.

request.name: set_unmanaged
request.description: The client draws the whole window, frame included. Without this a placed toplevel is still decorated by the compositor, around the position given.

request.name: activate
request.description: The client's window system activated this window. The compositor moves the keyboard focus to it (and from whatever had it).

event.name: origin

description.summary: where the compositor shows the surface

event.description:
The position, in output pixels, of the surface's top-left corner as the compositor currently shows it and hit-tests it. Surface-local pointer positions sent after this event (wl_pointer.enter, motion) are relative to this point, until the next origin event.
It is not always the position last set: a compositor shows a move some time after the request, and pointer events go on meanwhile, relative to where the surface was. A client turning surface-local positions into its own window system's coordinates adds this origin, not the position it last asked for; one that has not been sent an origin yet adds the position it asked for.
Sent when the shown position changes, before the pointer events that depend on it. A compositor may never send it, and a client then goes on adding the position it asked for.
